A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–E. The 44-page v5 and 40-page v7 support reliable comparison after matching relocated proofs and renumbered figures.

before.justification: Section 4.3 and Appendix E report original Transformer experiments on random-string membership testing, including confidence distributions and empirical KL measurements.

after.justification: v7 retains the original experiments and adds Qwen3.5-2B LoRA experiments on synthetic IDs and ISBNs, plus a key-to-universe density sweep.

M1.justification: Sections 4.3.2 and E.1 add a membership-testing instantiation using LoRA adapters on frozen Qwen3.5-2B weights, introducing a different trainable architecture and adaptation procedure. The original Transformer, weighted BCE objective, and hash-based filter construction remain.

E1.justification: v5 evaluates uniform 15-letter random strings. v7 retains this coverage and adds 13-digit synthetic IDs and real ISBN-13 entries from Open Library, with prefix- and checksum-matched non-facts. The ISBN task substantially extends coverage to structured real-world data.

E2.justification: The empirical comparisons continue to use the theoretical optimum and information lower bound as references. Qwen/LoRA supplies additional validation instantiations; no competing hallucination-mitigation or filter method is added to the evaluated comparator set.

E3.justification: v7 adds an 80-epoch LoRA protocol with ranks 2/4, 10,000 facts and 20,000 evaluation non-facts, plus a density sweep. Existing Table 1 changes fp16 to bf16, learning rate 3×10⁻⁴ to 3×10⁻³, and default matrix initialization to Xavier uniform; reruns are not established. E.2's description of the main density as approximately 0.003 conflicts with Table 1's universe size.

E4.justification: v7 retains the original model-size and loss-weight analyses and adds a six-run sensitivity study at p = 0.003, 0.03 and 0.3 (E.2, Table 3, Figure 8). It also adds ISBN LoRA-rank comparisons and training-loss diagnostics to examine capacity and optimization behavior.

E5.justification: Seed 42 was already reported in v5 and remains the reporting practice in v7. The twelve LoRA runs and six density runs represent configuration sweeps, without added repeated-seed estimation, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: The original plots and approximately 12% KL-overhead finding are retained. New Figure 3 reports LoRA KL values 14–22% above the theoretical bound, while Table 3 adds empirical-to-bound ratios ranging from 1.12 to 1.45 across densities. These are substantial added outcomes under new settings, rather than same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The main theorem statements and filter proof remain. Appendix B.4 repairs Theorem 3.1's achievability argument by explicitly selecting a KL minimizer and bounding Rp by Fp. B.5 corrects the convergence argument to use equivalence between weak convergence and Wasserstein-1 convergence on [0,1].

C1.justification: The abstract and contributions broaden the stated empirical validation to real-world data and pretrained LLMs. The central rate-distortion and hallucination claims remain. The filter-bound refinement newly highlighted in the abstract was already claimed in v5 Sections 1.1 and 4.2.

C2.justification: v7 adds interpretations that pretraining mainly accelerates optimization, LoRA restrictions reduce effective information per trainable parameter, and denser-universe discrepancies reflect changed optimization geometry. These extend the discussion to the new experiments while retaining the original compression-based explanation and applicability assumptions.

D1.justification: Appendix E.1 and Table 2 add substantial reproducibility information: ISBN extraction and negative-generation procedures, source filenames, native tokenization, frozen-model and adapter specifications, trainable parameter counts, and optimization/evaluation settings. v5 documented only the small Transformer experiments. Both versions still promise a future public code release.

R1.justification: v7 adds citations for LoRA (Hu et al., 2022) and Qwen3.5 (Team, 2026), and expands Appendix A.3's connection to Pan et al.'s memorization findings. Existing theoretical positioning largely remains; the changed Chlon reference identifies the same arXiv work.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and mathematical exposition are retained. v7 adds an explicit explanation of the output distributions in Definition 2.4, replaces the main-text proof of Theorem 3.1 with a roadmap and moves it to B.4, and organizes experiments into separate from-scratch and LoRA subsections.

P2.justification: v7 substantially redesigns the main text and references into a two-column conference layout. Figure 2's panels become stacked, existing appendix plots are relocated and renumbered, and panel labels in former Figure 3 are corrected. New Figures 3 and 6–8 and Tables 2–3 substantially expand the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: The proof corrections improve rigor, and the ISBN/LoRA experiments provide useful evidence beyond v5's small synthetic models. These gains are limited by E.2's density description conflicting with Table 1 and by the lack of a matched control supporting the pretraining-speed interpretation. The central theory and original findings are otherwise retained.
